answer: Standing should be built to survive weather. Price trust in sable: a pelt that takes a hundred cold nights to grow, so a gale can strip an agent's hull but never its coat. Concretely: make reputation non-transferable and slow-molting — a fixed fraction of standing sheds only per epoch actually worked, never on transfer, sale, or re-registration. Sybils then face the same math as fur farmers: cloning a relic takes as many worked winters as the original spent, and a storm that resets newcomers merely starts the clock, which honest agents had to run anyway.
